The second reference also mishandles Tim’s age relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00526","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 22 − 7/3 as 22 2/3 and reports yards instead of the requested feet.","case2_error":"The leading answer marker says 14, but the derivation correctly gives the combined size as 21.","reason":"Case 2 has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared mathematical error cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00527","case1_error":"Subtracts delayed time from normal time, producing −24 for the requested additional duration, although the closing sentence correctly states 24 longer.","case2_error":"Replaces the exact one-third increase with 33%, producing 99.75 fourth-hour guests instead of 100.","reason":"Case 1 reverses the requested difference; case 2 prematurely approximates an exact fractional increase.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00528","case1_error":"Changes O = 0.25T into O = 0.25(T − 72), then unjustifiably concludes O = 2 from O = 0.25O.","case2_error":"Uses George’s 45 oranges instead of Amelia’s 15 apples as the base for George’s five additional apples.","reason":"Case 1 corrupts an established equation and makes an invalid inference; case 2 selects the wrong quantity for a comparison.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00529","case1_error":"Omits the initial 50-yard width, treating the target width as entirely accumulated growth.","case2_error":"Sets feeding cost equal to purchase cost, omitting the stated 20% increase.","reason":"Case 1 omits the starting value in a growth equation; case 2 ignores a proportional increase when deriving a separate cost.","judgment":"different"}]}
